goal_text: (Reused from research_synth_029) Compare five continual learning approaches — Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), Progressive Neural Networks, Gradient Episodic Memory (GEM), PackNet, and Learning without Forgetting (LwF) — on their forgetting prevention mechanism, memory overhead, and whether they support backward transfer.

inputs.topic: continual learning catastrophic forgetting methods comparison

ground_truth: EWC (Kirkpatrick et al. 2017): quadratic penalty on weight changes weighted by Fisher information; low memory overhead (only Fisher diagonal); no backward transfer. Progressive Neural Networks: adds a new column per task with lateral connections to frozen prior columns; no forgetting by construction; no backward transfer; model grows linearly. GEM (Lopez-Paz & Ranzato): episodic memory stores old-task samples, constrains gradient updates to not increase old-task loss; requires storing replay buffer; supports approximate backward transfer. PackNet (Mallya & Lazebnik): iterative weight pruning frees capacity for new tasks with binary task masks; no memory of old data needed; no backward transfer. LwF (Li & Hoiem): knowledge distillation on new-task data preserves old-task output distributions; no old-data storage; limited backward transfer possible.
